newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate bond players sigh relief after FOMC.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate bond players sigh relief after FOMC.

text.p: U.S. corporations cheered by news of the Federal Reserve's decision to leave interest rates unchanged are expected to capitalize on lower rates and resume their financing plans, dealers said.
"You'll see some names trickle out in bits and pieces of details but not much is expected to happen until after the holiday," said one high-grade syndicate source.
On Tuesday, the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), the Fed's policy-setting arm, voted to leave interest rates unchanged.

Other players said the Fed's decision to leave interest rates unchanged has provided issuers with a window of opportunity for getting their financing needs met, as many still believe a tightening is on the horizon.

"With the Fed's decision not to tighten credit, I think the market interprets this to mean that there's going be to one later on, so it'll depend on what comes out of the (FOMC) minutes," another high-grade syndicate source said.
Meanwhile, among the first to line up to tap the market was Associates Corp with its sale of $300 million in four-year debt to yield 6.8285 percent.
The deal was won via competitive bid by JP Morgan Securities Inc.

Meanwhile, the bulk of this week's new issue activity is seen coming from the private placement market with about $1.0 billion in new deals slated to price mid-week, high-yield syndicate sources said.
Among upcoming issuers is Integrated Health Services Inc, which is slated to bring $250 million in 10-year 144A senior subordinated notes via Salomon Brothers, sources said.
Magnum Hunter Resources Inc is expected to sell $125 million in 10-year 144A senior notes via First Union, sources said.
Another $100 million in five-year 144A notes is expected from Navistar Financial Corp via JP Morgan Securities.
Energy Corp of America will bring $200 million in 10-year 144A senior subordinated notes via Chase Securities. The deal was upped from an initial $150 million, sources said.
DGS INternational Finance Co BV is also expected to bring a US$150 10-year 144A guaranteed notes via BT Securities.
Also, Compania Lationomericana De Infraestructura Servicios (CLISA) is expected to issue $100 million in senior seven-year 144A guaranteed notes via Citicorp Securities.
Intercel Inc is also expected to set $300 million in 10-year 144A senior notes via Morgan Stanley, sources said.
Among other high-yield offerings, Chief Auto Parts Inc, an auto parts retailer, is slated to bring $125 million eight-year senior notes via CS First Boston.
Looking ahead, a calendar is building for high-grade issues next week as players delay business until after the holiday.
The market will see an early close on Friday ahead of next Monday's Memorial Day holiday when U.S. financial markets will remain closed.

Among upcoming debt offerings Tandy Corp, a Fort Worth, Texas-based retailer of consumer electronics and computers, is expected to tap the market with a $200 million 10-year debt issue via Bear Stearns & Co, sources said.
Also, Frontier Corp, a telephone long distance carrier, is slated to bring a $300 million A3/A rated seven-year debt deal via Salomon Brothers.

Briggs & Stratton Corp, a maker of engines for lawn and garden equipment, is also expected to sell $100 million in 10-year debt and $75 million in five-year debt via Credit Suisse First Boston, sources said.

Another $600 million three-part debt offering from Hartford Insurance is expected to hit the market next week, sources said. The deal is expected to include seven-year, 10-year and 30-year maturities, they said.
In the government market, the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond is trading off 14/32 at 96-2/32 to yield 6.94 percent.
(( -- Nancy Leinfuss, 212-859-1675 ))
